default.description: Desktop capability for the main window (tray, folder picker, notifications, the updater). The shell talks to a server the user runs; it starts none. The `remote` URL list is what lets the window work in LOCAL mode, where the shell points the page at the backend it spawned on loopback: a page served over http is not the app's own origin, so without it every `plugin:window` command — dragging, minimize, maximize, close — and every app command below is refused there, which is a title bar with dead controls and an updater that never asks. Only loopback is granted: a server on the LAN or over Tailscale serves its own page and gets none of this (in REMOTE mode the shell loads its own assets instead, so the page is local to begin with and needs no grant).

mobile.description: Android/iOS capability for the main window: the mobile shell only hosts the web UI, so it gets the core commands and native notifications — no folder picker (no dialog permission) and no autostart, which do not exist there. The app commands are named here because the app manifest in build.rs makes every one of them ACL-checked on every platform: without these lines the iOS bridge (the two pushes the shell makes) and the shell's own state would be refused on the very platform they exist for.
